sections.sectionText: This course, designed to complement a concurrent internship, focuses on cultivating essential workplace writing, communication, and professionalization skills to support students’ professional growth and career readiness. Through activities and assignments, students will learn to set and achieve developmental goals, craft effective workplace communications, propose projects, provide meaningful updates, and present progress with confidence. Emphasizing proactive strategies and customized approaches, this course prepares students to excel in professional environments by enhancing their ability to adapt, articulate ideas, and contribute effectively to workplace success. This course is open to bachelor’s degree seeking students who have secured an internship. This course must be completed in the term in which the professional experience is completed.

restrictions: Restricted to students with Sophomore, Junior, or Senior class standing.
sections.sectionText: SP27 BTW 263 - Writing in the Disciplines - Game Writing and Design - This course teaches students to apply principles of procedural and expository writing to game design and game development. Similar to structure-based storytelling in screenplays, game creation requires a balance between creativity and practical application. Students will learn how to write proposals for games and/or interactive experiences with the goal of designing, developing, and building a working prototype along with a final draft of a game manual and strategy guide. No prior experience with coding is necessary to take this class. Restricted to Jr/Sr through Advanced Enrollment period; then any remaining seats will be available for So/Jr/Sr.

restrictions: Restricted to students with Sophomore, Junior, or Senior class standing.
sections.sectionText: SP27 BTW 263 - Writing in the Disciplines - Katrina Gaffney - Introduction to Literary Publishing - In this discussion- and market research-intensive class, students will investigate the contemporary literary publishing landscape with primary emphasis on literary magazines and a supplemental emphasis on book publishing. This class explores a survey of contemporary publishing, literary magazine production basics, and legal/ethical issues in publishing. As a complement to research and discussion, students will gain editorial experience reading for a print issue of Ninth Letter and including standard curatorial and editorial meeting practices. Successful students will understand the contemporary publishing landscape and its problems, careers paths in publishing, and basic literary magazine editorial work. They will gain practical experience working on an editorial team and develop prospective publishing career goals. Restricted to Jr/Sr through Advanced Enrollment period; then any remaining seats will be available for So/Jr/Sr.

restrictions: Restricted to students with Sophomore, Junior, or Senior class standing.
sections.sectionText: SP27 BTW 263 - Writing in the Disciplines - Andrew Moss - Effective Grant Writing - Students who take Effective Grant Writing will be prepared to work on a grant writing team, lead grant writing projects, and use their writing and research skills to secure funds for community projects. Students will participate in the entire grant writing cycle -- from researching funding opportunities to final submission -- and will work with local nonprofits to complete a polished grant on their behalf. The class will investigate the grant-writing process and its many genres and forms, including needs assessments, program assessments, letters of inquiry, RFPs (Requests for Proposals), and the most common sections of grant applications. Working with a team of peers and a community client, students will develop project management and collaborative writing skills. Students will explore the landscape of local grant-writing by meeting other grant-writing professionals and community organizations and use statewide and national databases and tools to identify current grant-writing trends and best practices. Students pursuing careers in social work, social services, or the nonprofit sector, or those who plan to work with state governments, local governments, or NGOs will benefit the most from this class, although the class is open to all majors and interests. Restricted to Jr/Sr through Advanced Enrollment period; then any remaining seats will be available for So/Jr/Sr.

title: Writing for Digital Media
info: Credit is not given toward graduation for BTW 360 and BTW 285. Prerequisite: Composition I.

sections.sectionText: SP27 BTW 360 - Writing for Digital Media - Students will build a professional online web presence and familiarize themselves with social media management. Explores how principles of effective composition and writing as a process interact with different, increasingly popular digital media. In addition to hands-on activities and practice with digital design and web development techniques, students will create social media campaigns, write reports that visualize data, and analyze the diverse audiences that make up the internet. Credit is not given toward graduation for BTW 360 and BTW 285. Prerequisite: Composition I.

sections.sectionText: An introduction to English grammar and linguistics, including: phonetics and phonology; morphology; syntax; semantics and pragmatics; sociolinguistics; language policy; writing; language acquisition; psycholinguistics and cognitive linguistics. Models and encourages a descriptive, curious, dynamic approach to the study of (English) language. Requires students to consider and explore the significance and application of their learning to their current and future life, work, and interactions, including the teaching of English at the secondary level. Same as BTW 402. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
